title.title: Weak pure infiniteness and $\mathcal O_\infty$ absorption
title.subtitle: Claim: if every positive element is properly infinite, the C*-algebra is strongly purely infinite

beats.text: Kirchberg and Rørdam's notions of pure infiniteness for non-simple C*-algebras
Claim: if every positive element is properly infinite, they coincide
So separable nuclear algebras of this kind absorb $\mathcal O_\infty$

achievement.label: Kirchberg–Rørdam: is pure infiniteness strong?
statement: \text{every } a \ge 0 \text{ properly infinite} \Rightarrow A \text{ strongly purely infinite}
achievement.context: Before: special cases, e.g. Hausdorff primitive spectrum (Blanchard–Kirchberg 2004)
achievement.note: No exactness, unitality or simplicity needed; the weak version needs exactness

verify.detail: Both formal statements: individual strong infiniteness and the exact case
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

plain: Several definitions of algebras that endlessly copy themselves were thought different; the natural ones agree

voice.text: Kirchberg and Rørdam defined several kinds of pure infiniteness for non-simple C star algebras.
They asked how these compare. Do they agree?
Claimed: if every positive element is properly infinite, they coincide.
